summary.name: JoeBro
summary.one_liner: A native SwiftUI Mac (and source-only iPhone companion) AI assistant that stores chats, documents and memory locally and sends prompts to a model endpoint the user chooses.
use_cases: private chat with local models via Ollama
editing documents with agent assistance on a Mac
masking card numbers and API keys before sending prompts to a model
keeping AI memory as plain Markdown files
running a headless assistant backend on a Raspberry Pi
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a Mac workspace for chat and document editing, with a backend that ships inside the Mac app. Chats, documents, memory and API keys are stored on the Mac, while prompts go to whichever endpoint the user picks: a local Ollama model or a pasted API key. Memory is kept as plain Markdown files editable on the Mac or phone. Cloak Mode, on by default, swaps detected keys, passwords, emails and account numbers for placeholders before requests leave the backend. The page also mentions MCP server connections, multi-source research, IMAP and calendar use, and an iPhone companion that pairs to a Mac that must stay awake. The author runs their own instance headless on a Raspberry Pi, which they say is not a supported installer.
notable: Cloak Mode masks detected sensitive values before any model request, on by default
Memory stored as plain Markdown files the user can open and edit
Chats, documents and API keys stored locally on the Mac
Author runs a headless Raspberry Pi backend, separate from the documented Mac setup
caveats: Prompts still go to the chosen model endpoint; hosted inference is not local
Cloak Mode is a guardrail and does not guarantee every sensitive detail is removed
The iPhone pairing requires a Mac that remains open and awake; iPhone companion is source-only
